name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - run: go vet ./...
      - run: go test ./...
      - name: Docs are up to date
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_wrapper: false
      - run: |
          go generate ./...
          git diff --exit-code docs

name: Release

# Pushing a tag such as v0.1.0 publishes a release, which the Terraform
# Registry picks up. GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and PASSPHRASE are repository secrets;
# the key's public half is registered with the Registry.
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - id: import_gpg
        uses: crazy-max/ghaction-import-gpg@v6
        with:
          gpg_private_key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          passphrase: ${{ secrets.PASSPHRASE }}
      - uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6
        with:
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GPG_FINGERPRINT: ${{ steps.import_gpg.outputs.fingerprint }}

# Terraform provider for Superlog

Manage [Superlog](https://superlog.sh) alerts, dashboards, and synthetic checks with Terraform or OpenTofu.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    superlog = {
      source = "superloglabs/superlog"
    }
  }
}

provider "superlog" {
  # https://superlog.sh (EU, the default) or https://us.superlog.sh (US).
  endpoint = "https://superlog.sh"
}

resource "superlog_alert" "checkout_errors" {
  name        = "Checkout errors"
  source      = "logs"
  aggregation = "count"
  comparator  = "gt"
  threshold   = 50
  filter      = { service = "checkout", severity = "ERROR" }
}
```

Set `SUPERLOG_API_KEY` to an API key from **Settings → API keys** in Superlog. See the [documentation](docs/index.md) for every resource.

| Resource | What it manages |
| --- | --- |
| `superlog_alert` | Threshold alerts on logs, spans, or metrics |
| `superlog_dashboard` | Dashboards, their variables, and all of their widgets |
| `superlog_synthetic_check` | Scheduled HTTP checks |
| `superlog_slack_channel` (data source) | Looks up a Slack channel by name for an alert or check |

## Exporting what you already have

Superlog writes Terraform for existing objects, with an `import` block for each one, so `terraform apply` adopts them instead of creating copies:

```shell
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPERLOG_API_KEY" https://superlog.sh/api/v1/terraform | jq -r .hcl > superlog.tf
terraform init && terraform apply
```

**Copy as Terraform** on an alert, dashboard, or synthetic check page copies the same configuration for one object.

## Development

```shell
go test ./...                 # unit tests
go generate ./...             # regenerate docs/ (needs terraform on PATH)
```

Acceptance tests create real objects in the workspace of the API key:

```shell
TF_ACC=1 SUPERLOG_API_KEY=slk_... SUPERLOG_ENDPOINT=https://superlog.sh go test ./internal/provider -run TestAcc
```

To try a local build, point Terraform at it with `dev_overrides` in `~/.terraformrc`:

```hcl
provider_installation {
  dev_overrides {
    "registry.terraform.io/superloglabs/superlog" = "/path/to/go/bin"
  }
  direct {}
}
```

## Releasing

Push a tag such as `v0.1.0`. The release workflow builds and signs the binaries with goreleaser, and the Terraform Registry publishes the new version.

# Superlog Provider

Manage Superlog alerts, dashboards, and synthetic checks. Create an API key in Superlog under Settings → API keys. The provider acts as the member who created the key, in that key's workspace.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    superlog = {
      source = "superloglabs/superlog"
    }
  }
}

# Set SUPERLOG_API_KEY to an API key from Settings → API keys.
provider "superlog" {
  # https://superlog.sh for the EU region, https://us.superlog.sh for the US region.
  endpoint = "https://superlog.sh"
}
```

## Exporting existing configuration

Superlog can write Terraform for objects you already have. Use **Copy as Terraform** on an alert, dashboard, or synthetic check, or export the whole workspace with the API:

```shell
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPERLOG_API_KEY" https://superlog.sh/api/v1/terraform | jq -r .hcl > superlog.tf
```

The export includes an `import` block for each object, so `terraform apply` adopts the existing objects instead of creating copies. Secret header values of synthetic checks become sensitive variables to set. Pass `alertIds`, `dashboardIds`, or `syntheticCheckIds` (comma-separated) to export only some objects.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) A Superlog API key. Can also be set with the `SUPERLOG_API_KEY` environment variable.
- `endpoint` (String) The Superlog URL: `https://superlog.sh` for the EU region (the default) or `https://us.superlog.sh` for the US region. Can also be set with the `SUPERLOG_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

# superlog_slack_channel (Data Source)

A Slack channel alerts and synthetic checks can post to: a public channel, or a private channel the Superlog app is in.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "superlog_slack_channel" "alerts" {
  name = "alerts"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The channel name, with or without `#`.

### Optional

- `workspace` (String) The Slack workspace's name. Needed when more than one connected workspace has a channel with this name.

### Read-Only

- `channel_id` (String)
- `integration_account_id` (String)
- `private` (Boolean)

--- # generated by https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-docs page_title: "superlog_synthetic_check Resource - superlog" subcategory: "" description: |- An HTTP check that requests a URL on a schedule and checks the response. After failures_to_alert failed runs in a row it posts to its Slack channel, and posts the recovery in the same thread. --- # superlog_synthetic_check (Resource) An HTTP check that requests a URL on a schedule and checks the response. After `failures_to_alert` failed runs in a row it posts to its Slack channel, and posts the recovery in the same thread. ## Example Usage ```terraform variable "health_token" { type = string sensitive = true } resource "superlog_synthetic_check" "api_health" { name = "API health" url = "https://api.example.com/health" interval_seconds = 60 failures_to_alert = 2 headers = { Accept = "application/json" } secret_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer ${var.health_token}" } assertions = [ { kind = "status_code", op = "eq", value = "2xx" }, { kind = "json_path", key = "$.status", op = "eq", value = "ok" }, { kind = "response_time", op = "lt", value = "1500", severity = "degraded" }, { kind = "certificate_expiry", op = "gt", value = "14", severity = "degraded" }, ] } ``` ## Schema ### Required - `name` (String) - `url` (String) The full HTTP or HTTPS URL to request. ### Optional - `assertions` (Attributes List) Checks on the response. Without any, a run passes when the request completes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assertions)) - `body` (String) The request body. Not for `GET` or `HEAD`. - `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled check does not run. Defaults to `true`. - `failures_to_alert` (Number) Failed runs in a row before the check posts to Slack, from 1 to 10. Defaults to 1. - `follow_redirects` (Boolean) Defaults to `true`. - `headers` (Map of String) Request headers by name. - `interval_seconds` (Number) How often the check runs: 60, 300, 900, 1800, or 3600 seconds. Defaults to 300. - `method` (String) Defaults to `GET`. - `retries` (Number) Immediate retries before a run counts as failed, from 0 to 2. Defaults to 1. - `secret_headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Request headers stored encrypted, such as `Authorization`. Superlog never returns their values, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected. - `slack` (Attributes) The Slack channel the check posts to. Look it up with the `superlog_slack_channel` data source. Without one, the check only records its history in Superlog. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slack)) - `timeout_ms` (Number) From 1000 to 30000. Defaults to 10000. ### Read-Only - `id` (String) The ID of this resource. - `web_url` (String) The check in Superlog. ### Nested Schema for `assertions` Required: - `kind` (String) `status_code`, `response_time` (ms), `header`, `body`, `json_path`, or `certificate_expiry` (days). - `op` (String) `status_code` takes `eq`, `neq`, `lt`, `gt`; `response_time` `lt`; `header` `eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `exists`, `not_exists`; `body` `contains`, `not_contains`; `json_path` all of these; `certificate_expiry` `gt`. Optional: - `key` (String) The header name for `header`, or the JSON path for `json_path`, such as `$.status`. - `severity` (String) A failed `critical` assertion fails the run; a `degraded` one marks it degraded. Defaults to `critical`. - `value` (String) Compared with the response. A status code may be a class such as `2xx`. ### Nested Schema for `slack` Required: - `channel_id` (String) The Slack channel ID. - `integration_account_id` (String) The Superlog Slack integration the channel belongs to. ## Import Import is supported using the following syntax: The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example: ```shell # Import a check by its ID, from its URL in Superlog. Secret header values # are not returned, so the first apply after an import sets them again. terraform import superlog_synthetic_check.api_health 55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555 ```

--- # generated by https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-docs page_title: "superlog_dashboard Resource - superlog" subcategory: "" description: |- A dashboard over the workspace's telemetry. The resource owns all of the dashboard's widgets: widgets added in Superlog are removed on the next apply. --- # superlog_dashboard (Resource) A dashboard over the workspace's telemetry. The resource owns all of the dashboard's widgets: widgets added in Superlog are removed on the next apply. ## Example Usage ```terraform resource "superlog_dashboard" "checkout" { name = "Checkout" variables = [ { name = "env" label = "Environment" attribute_key = "deployment.environment" options = ["production", "staging"] default_value = "production" }, ] widgets = [ { title = "Errors by service" type = "timeseries_count" # $${env} is the `env` variable; $$ keeps Terraform from reading it. config = jsonencode({ source = "logs" groupBy = "service.name" filter = { resourceAttrs = [{ key = "deployment.environment", value = "$${env}" }] } }) layout = { x = 0, y = 0, w = 6, h = 4 } }, { title = "Request duration p95" type = "timeseries_metric" config = jsonencode({ metricName = "http.server.duration", aggregation = "p95", unit = "duration_ms" }) layout = { x = 6, y = 0, w = 6, h = 4 } }, { title = "Recent errors" type = "log_table" config = jsonencode({ source = "logs", filter = { resourceAttrs = [{ key = "severity", value = "ERROR" }] } }) layout = { x = 0, y = 4, w = 12, h = 6 } }, ] } ``` ## Schema ### Required - `name` (String) ### Optional - `variables` (Attributes List) Dropdowns shown on the dashboard. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables)) - `widgets` (Attributes List) The dashboard's widgets, in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--widgets)) ### Read-Only - `id` (String) The ID of this resource. - `url` (String) The dashboard in Superlog. ### Nested Schema for `variables` Required: - `name` (String) Widgets use the selected value when a filter value is `$name` or `${name}`. Optional: - `attribute_key` (String) The attribute the variable usually filters, such as `deployment.environment`. - `default_value` (String) Must be one of `options` when there are any. - `label` (String) - `multi` (Boolean) Allows several values. Selecting none matches every value. - `options` (List of String) The choices. Leave it empty to type a value. ### Nested Schema for `widgets` Required: - `config` (String) The widget's settings as JSON; use `jsonencode`. For example `{ source = "logs", groupBy = "service.name" }`, `{ metricName = "http.server.duration", aggregation = "p95" }`, or `{ markdown = "..." }`. Filters go in `filter.resourceAttrs`. - `title` (String) - `type` (String) `timeseries_count` counts or aggregates logs or spans, `timeseries_metric` charts one metric, `log_table` and `trace_table` list matching logs or traces, and `markdown` shows text. Optional: - `layout` (Attributes) Position on a 12-column grid. Without it, the widget gets the standard size for its type below the others. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--widgets--layout)) Read-Only: - `id` (String) ### Nested Schema for `widgets.layout` Required: - `h` (Number) - `w` (Number) - `x` (Number) - `y` (Number) ## Import Import is supported using the following syntax: The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example: ```shell # Import a dashboard by its ID, from its URL in Superlog. terraform import superlog_dashboard.checkout 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 ```

--- # generated by https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-docs page_title: "superlog_alert Resource - superlog" subcategory: "" description: |- A threshold alert on logs, spans, or a metric. While the value is past the threshold, the alert posts once to its Slack channel and posts the recovery in the same thread. --- # superlog_alert (Resource) A threshold alert on logs, spans, or a metric. While the value is past the threshold, the alert posts once to its Slack channel and posts the recovery in the same thread. ## Example Usage ```terraform data "superlog_slack_channel" "alerts" { name = "alerts" } # More than 50 error logs from checkout in production in 5 minutes. resource "superlog_alert" "checkout_errors" { name = "Checkout errors" source = "logs" aggregation = "count" comparator = "gt" threshold = 50 filter = { service = "checkout" severity = "ERROR" attributes = [ { key = "deployment.environment", value = "production" }, ] } slack = { channel_id = data.superlog_slack_channel.alerts.channel_id integration_account_id = data.superlog_slack_channel.alerts.integration_account_id } } # p95 span duration above 750 ms, checked for each service. resource "superlog_alert" "slow_services" { name = "Slow services" source = "traces" aggregation = "p95" field = "duration" comparator = "gt" threshold = 750 window_minutes = 10 group_mode = "per_group" group_by = "service.name" } ``` ## Schema ### Required - `aggregation` (String) `count` counts matching logs or spans; `count_distinct`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `p50`, `p90`, `p95`, and `p99` read `field`. Metrics use `sum` or `avg`. - `comparator` (String) `gt` fires when the value is above `threshold`, `lt` when it is below. - `name` (String) - `source` (String) `logs`, `traces` (spans), or `metric`. - `threshold` (Number) ### Optional - `enabled` (Boolean) A disabled alert is not checked. Defaults to `true`. - `evaluation_interval_seconds` (Number) How often the alert is checked, from 60 to 3600 seconds. Defaults to 60. - `field` (String) What a log or span aggregation other than `count` reads: `duration`, an attribute key, or an AI usage field such as `ai:cost`. - `filter` (Attributes) Narrows the data the alert reads. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filter)) - `group_by` (String) The attribute key to split by when `group_mode` is `per_group`, such as `service.name`. - `group_mode` (String) `single` checks one total. `per_group` checks each `group_by` value and fires for each one separately. Defaults to `single`. - `metric_name` (String) The metric to read when `source` is `metric`. - `slack` (Attributes) The Slack channel the alert posts to. Look it up with the `superlog_slack_channel` data source. Without one, the alert only records its history in Superlog. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slack)) - `window_minutes` (Number) How many minutes of data each check reads, from 1 to 1440. Defaults to 5. ### Read-Only - `id` (String) The ID of this resource. - `url` (String) The alert in Superlog. ### Nested Schema for `filter` Optional: - `attributes` (Attributes List) Attribute filters. A key may start with `resource.`, `span.`, `log.`, or `field.`; a bare key is a resource attribute. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filter--attributes)) - `metric_kind` (String) Picks one metric when its name is sent as several kinds. - `metric_unit` (String) Picks one metric when its name is sent with several units. - `min_duration_ms` (Number) Only spans at least this long. - `service` (String) - `severity` (String) Log severity, such as `ERROR`. - `span_name` (String) - `status_code` (String) Span status code, such as `ERROR`. ### Nested Schema for `filter.attributes` Required: - `key` (String) - `value` (String) Optional: - `op` (String) `eq` (the default), `neq`, or `not_contains`. ### Nested Schema for `slack` Required: - `channel_id` (String) The Slack channel ID. - `integration_account_id` (String) The Superlog Slack integration the channel belongs to. ## Import Import is supported using the following syntax: The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example: ```shell # Import an alert by its ID, from its URL in Superlog. terraform import superlog_alert.checkout_errors 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 ```

version: 2
before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
builds:
  - env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    ldflags:
      - "-s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }}"
    goos: [freebsd, windows, linux, darwin]
    goarch: [amd64, "386", arm, arm64]
    ignore:
      - goos: darwin
        goarch: "386"
    binary: "{{ .ProjectName }}_v{{ .Version }}"
archives:
  - formats: [zip]
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
checksum:
  extra_files:
    - glob: terraform-registry-manifest.json
      name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_manifest.json"
  name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_SHA256SUMS"
  algorithm: sha256
signs:
  - artifacts: checksum
    args:
      - "--batch"
      - "--local-user"
      - "{{ .Env.GPG_FINGERPRINT }}"
      - "--output"
      - "${signature}"
      - "--detach-sign"
      - "${artifact}"
release:
  extra_files:
    - glob: terraform-registry-manifest.json
      name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_manifest.json"
changelog:
  disable: true
